text:
B: Hiya. Right, you're the one with the Ghibli postcard.
A: Erm, yeah, that's me. Hiya. Sorry, I'm Jodie. Is it just like, chatting again?
B: Apparently. Leanne. Stockport.
A: Walsall. Do you know what this pays, by the way? Nobody can tell me.
B: A voucher, I think. I'm doing it for the attention, to be honest.
A: Ha. Fair. So what do you do?
B: Graphic designer. Part-time, at a print and signage place. Menus, leaflets, shop fronts.
A: No way. That's literally what I did. Three years at a print place in Wednesbury, doing banners. I left in, like, November before last.
B: Why'd you leave?
A: Bored. And skint, honestly. Same banner, different car wash. So I'm doing an MA in UX now, at Birmingham City. Apps and websites and that. Proper money if I can get in.
B: UX. So, designing buttons for banks.
A: Nah, I don't think that's fair, to be honest. It's, like, problem-solving. Working out why people can't find stuff. It's not just buttons.
B: Sorry, but it is a bit buttons. I'm being a cow. I just, I'd hate it. All grey boxes and user journeys. I'd rather do a gig poster for nothing.
A: Yeah, well, gig posters don't pay my loan off, do you know what I mean? I want a nice house. I'm not gonna pretend I don't.
B: No, that's honest. I respect that more than people who say it's their passion.
A: Do you do your own stuff, then? I saw the prints on your wall, I loved them.
B: Thanks. Yeah, screen prints and riso zines. I sell them at craft fairs. I like weird stuff, old Soviet kids' books, Japanese pulp covers. That's the bit I actually care about.
A: Oh, I'd love to go to Japan. One day. When I've got money and I can face the flight.
B: I'm going before I'm forty-five. Gavin's not keen, but he'll come round. He's an electrician, he doesn't come round to anything fast.
A: Shut up. Ryan's a sparky.
B: Course he is. Does your house have a switch hanging off the wall?
A: The bathroom light's been flickering since March. He says it's "on the list."
B: The list. Gavin's got a list. Nothing on it gets done, but it's a lovely list.
A: Ha. And I've got a cat that knocks everything off my desk. Mabel. My stylus is somewhere under the radiator right now.
B: Moth does the same. She took a whole print off once, still wet.
A: Oh my God, we're the same person but older. Sorry, that came out wrong.
B: No, it didn't. It came out exactly right and I'm choosing to be offended.
A: Sorry! Erm, are you into true crime? You look like you would be.
B: Obviously. I listen to it while I'm printing.
A: It gives me anxiety but I can't stop. I watch it, then I'm checking the back door.
B: That's the point of it, isn't it. Reminds you you've locked up. Anyway, I'm having my tea after this, Gavin's doing chilli.
A: Ryan's on early starts so I do tea, which means chippy on Friday. Or a bap from the cafe if I'm at uni.
B: A bap. Bless you. It's a barm.
A: It's a bap, mate. Don't —
